newsitem.title: USA: Azeri president sees telecom privatization in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Azeri president sees telecom privatization in 1997.

text.p: Azeri President Haydar Aliyev on Thursday said his government planned to begin selling the state's telecommunications assets this year.
"They will be privatized," Aliyev told U.S. business executives in Washington. "We will start that privatization this year."
"Every foreign company can participate in the privatization," he said, speaking through an interpreter. "There are no barriers."
Azerbaijan began auctioning off state-owned assets last February, aiming to privatize 70 percent of all government enterprises, though it will leave the key oil sector in state hands.

About 100 executives attended the briefing by Aliyev, where he discussed investment opportunities in the former Soviet republic, urging American companies not just to focus on the potential $4 trillion in oil revenues there.
The United States accounts for only five percent of the foreign companies doing business in Azerbaijan. "It is not absolutely in the United States' interest to fall behind," Aliyev said.
He touted his country's favorable investment laws, including 10-year protections against any changes that might affect long-term contracts and no barriers to taking profits out of the country.
"The social and political situation in the country are very stable," said the leader, who took power in a military coup in 1993.

Azerbaijan's long-running conflict with Armenia is not impeding investment, Aliyev said. Still, he said, "if a durable peace is achieved ... then we can create more reliable conditions for investment in Azerbaijan."
The United States, Russia and France, mediating the bitter dispute between the two former Soviet republics, have said they are hoping for a settlement of the conflict this year.
